definitions.explanation: The process of a plant producing fruit.
Efforts, plans, or work producing successful results. Used figuratively to describe when sustained effort finally pays off.

examples.japanese: ⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{結実|けつじつ}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{受粉|じゅふん}→受粉：16612_jufun⟧⟦しない→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{結実|けつじつ}⟦しない→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{品種|ひんしゅ}→品種：11840_hinshu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Some varieties won't bear fruit without pollination.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{暖|あたた}かかった→暖かい：00618_atatakai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{結実|けつじつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{早|はや}かった→早い：00514_hayai⟧。
examples.english: It was warm this year, so the fruit set early.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{結実|けつじつ}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ようやく{結実|けつじつ}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{新薬|しんやく}→新薬：28055_shinyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{完成|かんせい}した→完成する：25528_kanseisuru⟧。
examples.english: The research finally came to fruition, and the new medicine was completed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{結実|けつじつ}し、⟦{条約|じょうやく}→条約：04912_jouyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{締結|ていけつ}→締結：13870_teiketsu⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The negotiations between the two countries bore fruit, and a treaty was concluded.

notes:
USAGE:
{結実|けつじつ} is used both literally for plants bearing fruit and figuratively for efforts producing results. The figurative sense is very common in writing and formal speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{結実|けつじつ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (efforts bear fruit)
- ⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{結実|けつじつ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (research comes to fruition)
- {結実|けつじつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (to see results)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{実|みの}る→実る：00282_minoru⟧ also means "to bear fruit" (both literally and figuratively) but is native Japanese (⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧) and sounds more natural in everyday speech. {結実|けつじつ} is Sino-Japanese and more formal.
